title: Geometric integrality over the separable Stein constants of a geometrically normal scheme
statement:
Let $l$ be a field and let $X$ be an integral proper finite-type $l$-scheme which is geometrically normal over $l$, meaning that every local ring of $X\times_l L$ is an integrally closed domain for every field extension $L/l$. Suppose that $e=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, with its structure inclusion from $l$, is a finite field extension of $l$, and that the canonical evaluation morphism $h:X\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ is proper with geometrically connected fibres: $X\times_e E$ is nonempty and connected for every field extension $E/e$. Then $e/l$ is finite separable, and $X$ is geometrically normal and geometrically integral over $e$.

More precisely, for every extension field $E/e$, the canonical morphism $X\times_e E\to X\times_l E$ is an open-and-closed immersion and $X\times_e E$ is a normal integral Noetherian scheme. The associated map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}(e\otimes_l E)$ is the inclusion of the component selected by multiplication $a\otimes t\mapsto at$.

Schemes, fields, integrality, properness, finite type, field extensions, separability, base change, normal rings, Noetherian rings and geometric integrality use [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], [def-pc-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Noetherian for a scheme means that it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. An open-and-closed immersion identifies its source with a subscheme whose underlying subset is both open and closed and whose local rings are those of the ambient scheme.

proof.text: For every field extension $L/l$, the local rings of $X_L$ are domains by hypothesis, hence have no nonzero nilpotents. Thus $X$ is geometrically reduced. Apply [lem-pc-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections-separable] to the proper $l$-scheme $X$ and the given field $e=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. It gives separability of $e/l$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]; finiteness was assumed. Since $e/l$ is finite, every $a\in e$ lies in the finitely generated algebraic subextension $l(a)$, whose only transcendence basis is empty, so separable generation of $l(a)/l$ says that $a$ is separable algebraic over $l$: $e/l$ is finite separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

Fix any $E/e$ and put $R=e\otimes_l E$, with $E$-algebra structure $t\mapsto1\otimes t$. Since $e/l$ is finite separable, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] show that $R$ is etale over $E$ (interchange the tensor factors). Multiplication $\mu:R\to E$, $a\otimes t\mapsto at$, is an $E$-algebra retraction. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting], there is an idempotent $p\in R$ with $\mu(p)=1$, $\ker\mu=(1-p)R$, and $R\cong E\times(1-p)R$, with $\mu$ the first projection. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}\mu$ includes precisely the clopen component $D(p)\cong\operatorname{Spec}E$.

proof.text: For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, give $A$ its $e$-algebra structure by restricting global functions. The affine base-change formula gives $U\times_l E=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_l E)$. The balanced inverse maps $a\otimes(b\otimes t)\mapsto ab\otimes t$ and $a\otimes t\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes t)$ identify $A\otimes_e R$ with $A\otimes_l E$. Pulling back the factor $R\to E$ therefore gives $A\otimes_e E$, the ring of $U\times_e E$. Explicitly, its kernel in $A\otimes_e R$ is generated by $1-p$, and its spectrum is $D(1\otimes p)$, with complementary open $D(1-1\otimes p)$. These identifications agree on overlaps because they are induced by the same structural maps. They prove that the canonical $X\times_e E\to X\times_l E$ is an open-and-closed immersion, and identify it with the pullback of the multiplication component.

proof.text: The local rings of $X\times_e E$ are consequently local rings of the geometrically normal $X\times_l E$, hence normal domains. Since $E/e$ was arbitrary, $X$ is geometrically normal over $e$. Also, a finite affine $l$-cover of $X$ remains a finite affine cover as an $e$-scheme; any finite set of $l$-algebra generators of a chart is also a set of $e$-algebra generators. Hence $X$ is of finite type over $e$. The base changes of these charts have rings $A\otimes_e E$, generated over $E$ by $a_i\otimes1$ for the chosen generators $a_i$ of $A$. Thus each $X\times_e E$ is of finite type over $E$.

source.place: Tag 038M, definition-geometrically-normal; finite-type verification directly from affine generators

proof.text: The given geometric connectedness of $h$ says exactly that every $X\times_e E$ is nonempty and connected. Fix $E/e$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}E$ is Noetherian (the only ideals of a field are $(0)$ and $(1)$), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and the finite type over $E$ verified in step 4 show that $X\times_e E$ is Noetherian. By step 4 all its local rings are normal domains. By [rem-pc-regular-normal] (2), the irreducible components of $X\times_e E$ are pairwise disjoint open and closed subsets which, as open subschemes, are normal and integral. As $X\times_e E$ is nonempty it has a component, which is a nonempty open and closed subset; connectedness forces it to be all of $X\times_e E$. Hence $X\times_e E$ is a normal integral Noetherian scheme. Since $E/e$ was arbitrary, $X$ is geometrically integral over $e$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and with step 4 every asserted clause is proved.
